title: Quantum codes from classical annealing
authors: Michael A. Perlin, Matthew Steinberg, Ben Criger
abstract: We introduce an adaptive simulated annealing algorithm to search for moderately-sized quantum error-correcting codes with high encoding rates and large distances. Our search targets two classes of stabilizer codes: (1) CSS codes, and (2) a subclass of CSS codes that we call ``self-dual with equivalent logicals'' (SWEL) codes, the latter of which which admit transversal implementations of logical Hadamard and phase gates that can be leveraged to construct fault-tolerant gate sets. The search is guided by an energy function that acts as a surrogate for the logical error rate in a code-capacity noise model, combining code distance with a count of minimum-weight logical operators to resolve the discrete plateaux that impede naïve distance optimization. For block lengths of up to $50$ physical qubits, our search finds state-of-the-art CSS and SWEL codes whose distances frequently meet or exceed the variants of the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound. In addition to providing favorable seed codes for fault-tolerant architectures based on code concatenation, the codes found in this work are promising candidates for high-rate code demonstrations on near-term quantum computing hardware.
summary: This paper introduces an adaptive simulated annealing method to efficiently search for high-performing quantum error-correcting codes, focusing on CSS and SWEL types. By optimizing a surrogate energy function related to logical error rates, the authors discover state-of-the-art codes whose parameters approach theoretical bounds. These findings provide promising candidates for building fault-tolerant quantum computation circuits.
main_problem: The primary goal is searching for quantum error-correcting codes that possess both high encoding rates and large distances.
main_result: The authors found state-of-the-art CSS and SWEL codes whose distances meet or exceed the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound for small block lengths (up to 50 qubits).
method: An adaptive simulated annealing algorithm is employed, guided by an energy function that approximates the logical error rate in a code-capacity noise model.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum stabilizer codes, specifically CSS codes and a subclass called SWEL codes. These are defined over physical qubits and characterized by their parity check matrices ($H$).
key_observables: Code distance ($d$), encoding rate ($k/n$), and the ability of logical gates to be implemented transversally.
important_parameters: Block lengths up to 50 physical qubits; code parameters $(n, k, d)$; quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound variants.
main_assumptions: The search relies on simulated annealing as a heuristic optimization technique due to the exponentially large space of possible codes. The search for automorphisms in related work is noted as non-exhaustive.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, reviews theoretical bounds (Hamming, QGV), details the adaptive simulated annealing optimization strategy using an energy function surrogate, and presents results on finding high-performing CSS and SWEL codes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental resource limitations in quantum computation by providing concrete constructions of highly efficient error-correcting codes suitable for near-term hardware demonstrations.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Logical error rates (LER) and discard rates (DR) per logical qubit (LQ) for the codes in Table 1 in a code-capacity noise model with a lookup table decoder. The decoder declares failure (triggering a discard) if it observes a syndrome that cannot be caused by any error of weight w < d/2. The physical error rate corresponds to the IID probability that each qubit is subject to a randomly chosen X, Y , or Z error.
